Location: app/controllers/application_controller.rb:159 (RIGHT)

Fallback locales are only ensured loaded in the HTTP request cycle, so server-side fallbacks silently fail in jobs/mailers

Trigger: A Sidekiq job or mailer (e.g. app/jobs/base.rb sets `I18n.locale = SiteSetting.default_locale`, PostAlerter uses `I18n.with_locale(user.effective_locale)`) translates a key that is missing in the active non-English locale; the fallback locales (site default / :en) were never loaded because `ensure_loaded!` is only invoked from ApplicationController#set_locale, and the patched `Base#load_translations` no-ops on the Simple backend's lazy `init_translations`, so unloaded fallback locales just return nil

Impact: Background-generated content (notification emails, digests, system posts) shows 'translation missing: ...' instead of falling back to the site default locale or English, defeating the feature this PR introduces for all non-request code paths

Evidence: I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!

Suggested fix: Move fallback loading into the translation path itself, e.g. have the accelerator's `translate` (or `load_locale`) call `I18n.fallbacks[locale].each { |l| ensure_loaded!(l) }` instead of relying on a controller before_filter

Location: config/initializers/i18n.rb:17 (RIGHT)

Fallback chain depends on SiteSetting.default_locale but the LRU translation cache key does not, causing wrong cached translations across multisite sites or after a default-locale change

Trigger: A multisite process serves two sites with different `SiteSetting.default_locale` (or an admin changes default_locale at runtime); a key missing in the user locale is translated on one site, cached in the accelerator's LRU cache under `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`, then the same key/locale is requested in the other site's context

Impact: The second site is served the first site's fallback translation (e.g. German text on a French-default site), or stale fallback text persists after the default locale is changed, because the cache key omits the default_locale component of the newly locale-dependent result

Evidence: [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact

Suggested fix: Include the resolved fallback chain (or SiteSetting.default_locale) in the accelerator cache key, or clear/namespace the cache per site and on default_locale changes

Trigger: Running the existing test suite: spec/integrity/i18n_spec.rb only validates YAML structure, and no spec covers translate_accelerator or the new fallback ordering, so a regression in fallback resolution (e.g. wrong chain order, unloaded fallback locale, or the Fallbacks module not being included) passes CI

Impact: The core new behavior — missing keys resolving via user locale → site default locale → :en — is unverified, so regressions in fallback resolution or lazy loading would ship undetected

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

          dayjs(override.end).utc().add(offset, "minute").minute(),

Trigger: While a victim has an in-progress GitHub install pipeline, an attacker gets the victim's browser to request /extensions/github/setup/?installation_id=<attacker_id>&state=<anything>. Location: public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/querySplitting.test.ts:85 (RIGHT)

Test asserts $__auto is interpolated to '5m' although production applyTemplateVariables deliberately excludes __auto from frontend interpolation

Trigger: The mock templateSrv.replace unconditionally does input.replace('$__auto', '5m'), ignoring the variables map. The real applyTemplateVariables destructures __auto out of scopedVars ('We want to interpolate these variables on backend'), so in production the expr keeps $__auto and only the backend replaces it.

Impact: The test certifies behavior ($__auto interpolated in expr before execution) that the production code path intentionally does not perform, giving false confidence and masking regressions in the actual pass-through semantics; a future reader may rely on this assertion as documented behavior.

Evidence: expect(jest.mocked(datasource.runQuery).mock.calls[0][0].targets[0].expr).toBe('count_over_time({a="b"}[5m])');

Suggested fix: Assert only the behavior the frontend actually changes (e.g. step: '$step' -> '5m'), or make the mock replace honor the passed variables map so $__auto stays uninterpolated as in production.

Location: public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/querySplitting.ts:299 (RIGHT)

Queries are interpolated twice: runSplitQuery and DataSourceWithBackend.query both apply applyTemplateVariables, duplicating ad-hoc filters

Trigger: A user runs a Loki query with the lokiQuerySplitting feature toggle enabled while ad-hoc filters are active on the dashboard/Explore. runSplitQuery interpolates the targets here, then each sub-request flows through datasource.runQuery -> super.query() (DataSourceWithBackend.query, line 185), which calls applyTemplateVariables again with the same request.filters.

Impact: addAdHocFilters is executed twice on the same expression, so the query sent to Loki contains every ad-hoc label matcher/label filter duplicated (e.g. {a="b", x="y", x="y"}). It also re-runs templateSrv.replace on already-interpolated text, so variable values that themselves contain '$name' tokens get recursively re-interpolated.

Evidence: .map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters));

Suggested fix: Apply interpolation in only one layer: either strip request.filters/scopedVars from the sub-requests passed to runQuery so DataSourceWithBackend does not re-apply them, or mark targets as already interpolated (e.g. keep interpolation only in DataSourceWithBackend and interpolate only step/expr needed for calculateStep locally without adding ad-hoc filters).

Trigger: The test's replace mock does input.replace('$__auto', '5m') regardless of the variables argument, but the real applyTemplateVariables removes __auto from scopedVars before calling templateSrv.replace, so production leaves $__auto in the expr for backend interpolation.

Impact: The assertion that the sub-request expr contains '[5m]' passes only because of the over-permissive mock; it does not verify real interpolation behavior for the shard path and can hide a regression where $__auto handling changes.

Evidence: expect(jest.mocked(datasource.runQuery).mock.calls[0][0].targets[0].expr).toBe(

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
